headline: New sanctions on major crude exporters tighten oil supply; Brent jumps 6%
summary: Western governments announced new sanctions on two major crude exporters overnight. Traders expect around 1.5 million barrels a day to leave the market, and Brent rose about 6% in early Asian trading.

headline: Treasury yields surge as Fed officials signal rates will stay higher for longer
summary: Three Federal Reserve officials said inflation progress has stalled and that rate cuts are not on the table this year. The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 25 basis points, its largest one-day move in months.

headline: Big Tech sells a record USD 45bn of bonds in a week to fund AI data centres
summary: Four of the largest US technology companies issued a combined USD 45bn of bonds last week, a record for the sector. Proceeds are earmarked for AI data centres and chips, and several deals priced at wider spreads than expected.

headline: Geneva watch auction sets a new record for a vintage chronograph
summary: A rare 1950s chronograph sold for a record price at a Geneva auction on Sunday. Organisers said bidding from Asian collectors was strong.

headline: Rates: we push back our first Fed cut call to mid-2027
summary: After Friday's Fed comments we no longer expect a rate cut this year or early next. We see the 10-year yield staying elevated and prefer the 1 to 3 year part of the curve.

headline: Energy: sanctions add a supply premium, airlines face higher fuel bills
summary: We raise our near-term Brent range. Integrated energy producers benefit directly, while airlines with limited fuel hedging face margin pressure.

headline: Reminder: e-banking maintenance window this weekend
summary: The e-banking platform will be unavailable from Saturday 22:00 to Sunday 06:00 SGT for scheduled maintenance. Trade instructions can still be placed by phone.

headline: REITs and long-dated bonds bear the brunt of the yield move
summary: Rate-sensitive assets fell sharply. Long-dated USD bonds lost around 3 to 4% and Asian REITs opened lower, while short-dated bonds were little changed.

headline: AI capex: credit investors start to ask for a higher premium
summary: Heavy bond supply is weighing on technology credit spreads and has spilled over into tech equities. Structured notes linked to large technology shares have moved closer to their barriers.

headline: Invitation: wealth planning webinar on family governance
summary: Our wealth planning team will host a webinar on family governance and succession on 22 October. Registration is open to clients and their advisers.

headline: China unveils new stimulus package aimed at consumption and property
summary: Beijing announced a package of consumer subsidies, property support and local government refinancing. Mainland and Hong Kong equity futures rose sharply ahead of the open.

headline: China stimulus: constructive on Asia, but follow-through matters
summary: The package is larger than the market expected and supports our modest overweight in Asia ex-Japan equities. We would build exposure gradually, as earlier rallies faded when implementation was slow.

headline: Oil sanctions widened to cover shipping and insurance; Brent extends gains
summary: The sanctions announced overnight were widened at midday to cover tankers and marine insurers. Brent extended its gain to about 10% on the day and jet fuel prices rose with it.

source: Partner bank A corporate action notice
headline: Partner Bank A to redeem its 5.875% USD perpetual at par on 12 November 2026
summary: Partner Bank A issued a call notice for its 5.875% USD perpetual bond. Holders will be repaid at par on 12 November 2026. The bond had traded around 96 because the market expected the call to be skipped.
